name: Islamabad International Airport
before:
Pakistan's largest and now busiest airport, 25 km south west of Islamabad and serving Rawalpindi as well. It took over as the country's busiest in the 2024-25 financial year, passing Karachi.

It is new. Full operations began on 6 May 2018, replacing Benazir Bhutto International, and the 180,000 square metre terminal is built for 9 million passengers and 80,000 tonnes of cargo a year, with room to grow to 25 million. There are 15 gates plus ten remote stands, 42 immigration counters, duty free and a food court.

It was the first airport in Pakistan with double airbridges able to handle an A380.

Road access is good in every direction. The Srinagar Highway connects to Islamabad and on to the M-1 for Peshawar, the GT Road runs to Rawalpindi, and a separate four lane highway was built for freight.

A third runway is planned, with the civil aviation authority acquiring 2,833 acres for it. The airport is a hub for Pakistan International Airlines and SereneAir.
after:
Islamabad International is one of Pakistan's two busiest airports, with Karachi. It lies 25 km south west of Islamabad and serves Rawalpindi as well.

Commercial flights began on 3 May 2018, when it replaced Benazir Bhutto International. The 180,000 square metre terminal was built for 9 million passengers a year, with room to grow to 25 million. It opened with 15 gates, airbridges able to take the Airbus A380, duty-free shops and a food court.

The airport is well served by main roads.

Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) and SereneAir both fly from here.

claims.claim: one of Pakistan's two busiest airports, with Karachi
claims.inAfter: Islamabad International is one of Pakistan's two busiest airports, with Karachi.
claims.note: Was 'now busiest'. Good sources disagree on the order. Wikipedia, on Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority figures for July 2024 to June 2025, puts Islamabad first (6,804,439 in its infobox) ahead of Karachi. ProPakistani (16 Feb 2026), on Pakistan Airports Authority figures for calendar 2025, puts Karachi first (8.5 million) and Islamabad second (7.87 million). Both agree the two are the busiest, so the text says only that. No figure is quoted: only one publisher of the 2025 numbers could be saved.
